commit.message:
Measured fidelity against a real NSGlassEffectView; fix the dark-appearance bias

First actual pixel-for-pixel comparison. A real NSGlassEffectView (macOS 27,
darkAqua, 160x88, cornerRadius 44) is rendered over the same hard 0x20|0xE0
backdrop the shader harness uses, captured window-scoped via ScreenCaptureKit,
and diffed against our render at identical geometry.

  before   MAE 32.05   PSNR 17.49 dB   mean delta +32.0
  after    MAE 10.03   PSNR 25.97 dB   mean delta  -4.8

MAE and mean delta being equal at 32.0 showed a pure offset, not noise: our
glass was uniformly ~12.5% too bright. platformContentGlass ships ONE colour
matrix, but a real view does not use the same bias in both appearances -- the
decoded clear variant measured bias 0.0966 dark vs 0.2795 light, ratio 0.346.
Applying that ratio to the regular bias gives 0.235 * 0.346 = 0.0813, which
removes the offset. RGB terms unchanged; only the additive bias differs.
Glass.regular now selects the matrix from the live appearance.

Two lessons recorded:
  * cacheDisplay() cannot capture glass -- it is composited by the window
    server, so the reference must be captured externally.
  * the vertex stage must map vUV to the RENDER TARGET half-size, not the
    element half-size, or the shape fills the whole target and the comparison
    is meaningless.

fidelity-vs-apple.png shows Apple, ours, and the 6x-amplified difference.
Residual -4.8 mean is now within the tone-curve behaviour the decode agents
found for regular-dark, which is not affine and remains unmodelled.
